transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’ve just been feeling like I’m becoming a burden, doctor. I don’t mean to sound dramatic. It’s just… I keep thinking my wife and the kids might be better off if I didn’t wake up. And I’ve caught myself saying I don’t need to see another winter. I know that probably isn’t the right sort of thing to say, but that’s what’s been bringing me in.
Have you ever felt this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced these kinds of thoughts and feelings?

It’s not exactly the first time, no… though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s been sort of hanging around since my bowling partner died—about a year and a month ago now, I think. I kept expecting it to ease up, but… well, it hasn’t really.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore that used to bring you joy, like maybe bowling or spending time with your family?

Yes… I suppose that’s fair to say. I used to look forward to things, you know—bridge, fussing around in the garden, helping with the church cooking, even going to Cubs games. Those were good things.

Lately I mostly just… sit in my chair. I tell myself I’ll get up and do something, but I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it. I’m sorry, that sounds pretty poor, doesn’t it? But yes, I’ve noticed that.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t been keeping track of my weight very carefully. My appetite… maybe it’s not quite what it used to be, but I don’t want to overstate it. I still eat some, especially if my wife puts something in front of me. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling like you’re worthless or guilty about things more than usual lately?

Yes… I suppose I have, more than I’d like to admit.

I keep turning things over in my head—every little thing I did wrong with him, and with my family. Things I should’ve said, or shouldn’t have said. I know maybe that sounds excessive, but it feels like I’ve been a pretty poor excuse for help to anyone.

Sometimes I think I’m just… no good to anybody. And that whatever punishment is coming, I probably deserve it. Is that… is that what you mean?
Have you felt more tired or noticed a lack of energy lately, even when you haven't been doing much?

I’m not sure I’d call it tired exactly… I mean, I am 80, so I suppose some slowing down is to be expected, isn’t it?

I do spend more time sitting than I used to, and I don’t seem to have much get-up-and-go. But I haven’t been doing much, so it’s hard to say if I’m tired or just… not pushing myself. Does that answer it alright?
Have you found it harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make too much of it, but it has been harder.

I used to help keep the numbers straight for the senior center budgets, and lately I just… I can’t seem to hold them in my head properly. And I’ll sit there with a bill, or look at the calendar, and half an hour can go by before I really understand what I’m supposed to be doing with it.

Maybe that sounds silly, but it’s been bothering me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a period in your life, before this most recent one, where you felt down or lost interest in things for two years or more?

I don’t think so… not for as long as two years, no.

I’ve had low spells, I suppose most people have by my age, but nothing I would describe as going on that long before this. At least, not that I can recall clearly. Is that helpful?
Would you say that your current low mood and loss of interest in things have been going on for more than two years now?

More than two years? No… I don’t think it’s been that long.

It really started after my bowling partner died — that was about a year and a month ago now. I’ve maybe not been quite myself since then. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when I’d say it began. Is that clear enough?

Between the time you had low spells before and the current period that started after your bowling partner’s death, would you say your mood returned to normal for a while, or did you feel down the whole time?

I think I did come back to myself in between, yes. I wouldn’t say I was down the whole time.

This current stretch… it’s really been since my bowling partner died, about a year and a month ago. That’s when things seemed to settle in and not lift the way they usually would. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Would you say that your current low mood and loss of interest in things have been present almost every day for the past two years, or has there been a time when you felt significantly better during this period?

No, not the past two years, I don’t think so.

It’s really been since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago. Since then it’s been hard to get back to feeling like myself. I hope that’s answering it the way you mean.
Would you say that your current low mood and loss of interest in things have been present almost every day for the past two years, without much relief?

No… not two years, no. I don’t think it’s been that long without relief.

Like I said, it’s been since my bowling partner died — about a year and a month ago. That’s when it really started and seemed to stay. I hope I’m answering that the right way.
Would you say that your current low mood and loss of interest in things have been present almost every day for the past two years, even before your bowling partner passed away?

No, I wouldn’t say it was almost every day for two years, or before he passed. It’s really been since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago. That’s when it started feeling like this and didn’t really lift. I hope that makes sense.
Would you say that your current low mood and loss of interest in things have been present almost every day for the past two years, even though you mentioned it started about a year and a month ago?

Right… yes, I guess that’s what I mean. Not two years, no. It’s been going on since my bowling partner died, about a year and a month ago. Since then it’s been pretty steady. Is that the way you’re asking it?
Would you say that your current low mood and loss of interest in things have been present almost every day for at least the past two weeks?

Yes… yes, I’d say at least the past two weeks. Really, it’s been going on since my bowling partner died, about a year and a month ago. It’s hard to admit that, but… I think that’s the honest answer. Is that what you mean?
